title: Physics-informed neural networks quantify perivascular CSF flow in mice
summary: Artificial intelligence velocimetry combined sparse particle-tracking velocity measurements with physics-informed neural networks to infer three-dimensional velocity, pressure and wall shear stress of cerebrospinal fluid in perivascular spaces. In four mice the abstract reports a mean speed of 16.33 +/- 11.09 um/s and a wall shear stress of 3.00e-3 Pa. Validation used 70% of measurements for training and agreement with the remaining 30%.

evidence.tested: Agreement with held-out 30% of particle-tracking measurements and sensitivity analyses of boundary inputs.
evidence.unknown: Four mice; validation uses held-out measurements from the same data; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Physics-informed neural networks inferring flow fields from sparse velocity measurements.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref where stated. Publisher full text not accessed.
